[AI engineering](../index.qmd) / Model behavior and context

Learn what the model sees, what you ask it to do, and how to tell whether a prompt change helped.

## What to understand

- **LLM basics:** tokens, embeddings, attention, training versus inference, context limits and probabilistic generation.
- **Instructions:** task boundaries, examples, output criteria and conflicting instructions.
- **Context engineering:** select evidence, order it, manage conversation state and avoid carrying irrelevant history.
- **Structured outputs:** schemas, validation, refusals and incomplete responses. Valid JSON does not establish factual correctness.
- **Model selection:** compare capability, quality, latency and cost on the same representative inputs.
- **Memory:** separate the current context from durable user preferences, retrieved records and workflow state.

## How the pieces connect

Prompting changes the instructions and context at inference time. Retrieval supplies evidence; fine-tuning changes model weights. They address different causes.

## A question to test

Compare a plain prompt, an example-based prompt and a structured-output version on the same small set of real tasks. Save failures and token usage.
